info.name: LedgerCore API
info.description: Every signed operation of the Ledger Core, Reconciliation and Webhooks APIs. Set apiKey and apiSecret in the environment (a credential from the console); each request is signed with the LC1-HMAC-SHA256 scheme of ADR-023 by the collection's pre-request script. Guides: /docs/guias/autenticacion.

exec: // Request signing of ADR-023 (scheme LC1-HMAC-SHA256) as a Postman
// pre-request script. It is plain ES5 so it runs in Postman's sandbox
// (which provides CryptoJS) and in node, where scripts/build-downloads.mjs
// same vectors the Go, TypeScript and PHP implementations pass.
// Everything above the "Postman wiring" marker is the signer; the code below
// it only reads the request and sets the four headers.
// Percent-decodes to bytes; plusIsSpace is the form-style rule for queries.
throw new Error("malformed percent-encoding in path or query");
// Percent-encodes every byte except the RFC 3986 unreserved characters.
for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) if (a[i] !== b[i]) return a[i] - b[i];
var k = eq < 0 ? part : part.slice(0, eq);
pairs.sort(function (a, b) { return lcCompare(a[0], b[0]) || lcCompare(a[1], b[1]); });
// input: method, host, path, rawQuery, idempotencyKey, apiKey, secret, timestamp, nonce, body (exact text sent)
return { bodySha256: bodySha256, canonical: canonical, signature: signature };
throw new Error("Set apiKey and apiSecret in the LedgerCore environment (a credential from the console).");
// The URL as it will be sent: variables resolved, then split by hand
// (Postman's sandbox has no WHATWG URL). The host keeps its port.
if (!m) throw new Error("Cannot read the request URL: " + resolved);

request.description: List ledgers
Create a ledger
Get a ledger

Replaces the metadata keys the ledger accepts: `transaction_keys` on
new transactions, holds and movements, `account_keys` on new accounts. A list
that is `null` or left out removes that allowlist (any key accepted);
an empty list accepts no key. A key outside the list is rejected with
422 `metadata_key_not_allowed`. Requires the `ledger:write` scope.

Every ledger, with or without an allowlist, accepts only scalar
values and rejects obvious personal data (see `Metadata`). The policy
governs metadata written from then on; what is already stored is not
re-judged. The change waits for the writes in flight on the ledger,
and writes that commit after it are judged by it.

Each change leaves an `audit_log` row (`ledger.metadata_policy.update`)
with the previous and the new policy, in the same database
transaction. Setting the policy the ledger already has is a no-op and
audits nothing.

item.name: Require an FX quote for conversions

request.description:
Turns the ledger's `require_fx_quote` on or off (off by default for
every ledger). While it is on, a transaction that holds more than one
asset is refused with 422 `fx_quote_required`, drafts included: a
plain transaction carries no quote, so convert with a posting group
(`POST /v1/posting-groups` with `fx`) or a transfer between ledgers
that cites `fx`. A transfer between ledgers that moves more than one
asset without `fx` is refused the same way when either of its two
ledgers has the policy on. Reversals, and replays of what was
accepted earlier, are never refused by it. Requires the `ledger:write`
scope.

The policy governs movements written from then on. The change waits
for the writes in flight on the ledger, and writes that commit after
it are judged by it. Each change leaves an `audit_log` row
(`ledger.fx_policy.update`) with the previous and the new value;
setting the value the ledger already has is a no-op and audits nothing.

item.name: Choose how a provider's loss is shared

request.description:
Sets the ledger's `loss_allocation` ([ADR-020](https://github.com/ASanchezT85/ledgercore/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-020-one-wallet-provider-exposure.md)
§6), the rule that says whose money is lost when a provider fails:

- `pro_rata_pool`: the loss is shared over every holder's balance, pro
  rata (safeguarded funds are one pool).
- `by_provider`: the loss falls on the holders whose money sat at that
  provider.

**There is no default.** A ledger that never set it returns
`loss_allocation: null`, has only the provider level
(`GET /v1/ledgers/{id}/provider-exposure`) and refuses the owner matrix
with 409 `loss_allocation_not_configured`: a silent default would pick
one side of a legal question for the tenant. Which rule applies to a
licence and country must be confirmed with counsel; this is not legal
advice. The field is required and cannot be unset.

The change waits for the writes in flight on the ledger. Each change
leaves an `audit_log` row (`ledger.custody_policy.update`) with the
previous value (`null` the first time) and the new one; setting the
rule the ledger already has is a no-op and audits nothing. Requires
the `ledger:write` scope.

item.name: Flag movements that stay open too long

request.description:
Sets the ledger's `stale_movement_after` ([ADR-019](https://github.com/ASanchezT85/ledgercore/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-019-staged-movements.md)
§8): how long a movement may stay open (not terminal) before it is
stale. A duration in Go syntax (`"720h"` for 30 days, `"90m"`), whole
seconds, from `1m` to `87600h`; `null` turns the check off, which is
the default. The field is required.

A sweeper in ledger-core (every `LEDGERCORE_STALE_SWEEP_INTERVAL`,
default 5 minutes) finds the open movements whose `opened_at` is
older than the setting, sets their `stale_at` and emits
`ledger.movement.stale` **once per movement**; reconciliation turns it
into a `movement_stale` exception that the movement's close resolves.
Lowering the setting reports the movements that now cross it on the
next sweep; a movement already reported is never reported again.
`GET /v1/movements?status=open&opened_before=…` lists the open ones of
any age.

Each change leaves an `audit_log` row (`ledger.movement_policy.update`)
with the previous and new value in seconds (`null` when off); setting
the value the ledger already has is a no-op. Requires the
`ledger:write` scope.

item.name: Ask console users for a fresh second factor above an amount

request.description:
Sets the ledger's `step_up_thresholds` ([ADR-030](https://github.com/ASanchezT85/ledgercore/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-030-step-up-by-amount.md)):
per asset, the gross amount in minor units (the sum of the
transaction's debits in that asset) at or above which a **console
user** must hold a step-up elevation to post. It applies to every
write that posts a transaction: a posted transaction, posting a
draft, a reversal, posting events and groups, ledger transfers (each
side against its own ledger) and executing an adjustment request.
Without the elevation the write answers `403 step_up_required` and
writes nothing. Signed requests with an API credential are never
asked: the signature, scopes and IP allow-list are their control.

`{}` turns step-up off, the default. At most 100 assets, each value
greater than zero. While a policy is on, changing or removing it also
needs the elevation, so a stolen session cannot switch it off first.
Each change leaves an `audit_log` row
(`ledger.step_up_policy.update`) with the previous and new
thresholds. Requires the `ledger:write` scope.

item.name: What each provider holds, and whether customer funds are backed

query.description: RFC 3339 instant; omit for the report as of now.

request.description:
The provider level of [ADR-020](https://github.com/ASanchezT85/ledgercore/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-020-one-wallet-provider-exposure.md)
§2, per provider and asset. It needs no `loss_allocation`, so it always
works. An account belongs to a provider when `metadata.provider` names
it or its path has a `provider` segment followed by the name
(`assets:provider:bank_x:custody`), as in `GET /v1/provider-positions`.

- `custody`: posted balance (debits - credits) of the provider's
  `asset` accounts with `fund_class: customer` and `liquidity: liquid`:
  the customer money physically there. Summed over providers it is
  `customer_assets` of `GET /v1/ledgers/{id}/coverage`.
- `claims`: the same with `liquidity: claim`. Reported apart; it never
  counts as backing.
- `own`: posted balance of the provider's `own` asset accounts: the
  platform's own money there (receivables included).
- `payable`: posted balance (credits - debits) of the provider's
  `liability` accounts: what the platform owes the provider.

`breaks` lists where customer funds are not backed, and `backed` is
`breaks` being empty:

- `ledger_shortfall` (per asset): customer assets do not reach customer
  liabilities, the `shortfall` of `/coverage`.
- `negative_custody` (per provider and asset): the provider's customer
  custody is below zero; a provider cannot hold negative money.

Per-provider backing has no owner meaning in a pool, so under
`pro_rata_pool` these are the whole check. Under `by_provider` it adds:

- `provider_shortfall` (per provider and asset): the holders' traced
  portions at the provider (the `by_provider` rows of
  `exposure-matrix`, transit included) are more than its customer
  assets (`custody` + `claims`). A fee the provider kept out of
  customer money (a settlement that delivered less than it took) shows
  here, at the provider that received less.

An account that names a provider is the provider's, never a holder's.

**As of a date.** Like `/coverage`: with `as_of` the sums are rebuilt
from the postings with `effective_at <= as_of`, using the `fund_class`
and `liquidity` each account had then. `loss_allocation` is today's.

item.name: Provider × holder matrix under the ledger's loss rule

query.description: RFC 3339 instant; omit for the matrix as of now.

request.description:
Whose money sits at which provider ([ADR-020](https://github.com/ASanchezT85/ledgercore/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-020-one-wallet-provider-exposure.md)
§2), computed on read under the ledger's `loss_allocation`, never
stored. It replaces N × M calls to read one wallet per provider.

- `pro_rata_pool`: holder h's exposure to provider P = `balance(h)` ×
  `custody(P)` / Σ customer custody, per asset. Only providers with
  positive customer custody weigh (a negative one is a `break` of
  `provider-exposure`; `claims` never weigh). The shares of a holder add
  up to its balance exactly (the cents go to the largest remainders).
- `by_provider`: a fold over the ledger's postings in commit order
  that keeps a portion per (holder, provider). Money in through P is
  P's; a debit of a holder takes from its portion at the provider the
  money leaves through first, then pro rata; P2P and stages into and
  out of a movement's transit carry the portions along; a treasury
  write with no holder leg (a settlement, a rebalance) moves every
  holder's portion at P to Q pro rata in one step. Which provider a
  stage belongs to comes from its movement (ADR-019), so a
  `complete` that only debits transit is still P's. Money no provider
  received yet (the bought currency of a conversion) is `unplaced`
  until treasury books it into a custody. The transit of movements in
  flight is in the `holder: ""` row.
- Not configured: 409 `loss_allocation_not_configured`. There is no
  default (`PUT /v1/ledgers/{id}/custody-policy`).

A holder is the `holder` of `metadata`, or the path segment after
`holder` (`liabilities:holder:ana:available`); its `balance` adds its
`liability` accounts with `fund_class: customer` and a positive
balance, `available`, `incoming` and the rest, in one asset. One in the
red never lowers it, as in `/coverage`. `holder: ""` gathers customer
liabilities that name no holder, so the rows add up to the
liabilities of `/coverage` (less accounts that name a provider).
`unplaced` is the part of a balance that no provider custody backs: all
of it when the asset has no positive customer custody.

The matrix is not paginated; every holder with a balance is returned.
`as_of` works as in `GET /v1/ledgers/{id}/coverage`.

query.description: RFC 3339 instant; omit for the report as of now.

request.description:
Whether the funds that back customer money cover what is owed to
customers, per asset of the ledger:

- `customer_assets`: posted balance (debits - credits) of the
  ledger's `asset` accounts with `fund_class: customer` and
  `liquidity: liquid` — the bank or safeguarding accounts that hold
  customer money and can pay it out now.
- `customer_claims`: posted balance of the `asset` accounts with
  `fund_class: customer` and `liquidity: claim` — money that may take
  years to collect (a receivable from a failed provider, say). Reported
  apart; it never counts as backing.
- `customer_liabilities`: posted balance (credits - debits) of its
  `liability` accounts with `fund_class: customer` — wallets and
  other balances owed to customers. Only accounts with a positive
  balance add to it: a wallet in the red (`allow_negative`) never
  lowers what is owed to the others.
- `customer_receivables`: the sum of the negative balances of those
  same accounts, as a positive number — what customers owe the
  platform. `negative_accounts` counts them. They are reported apart
  and never reduce `customer_liabilities` nor count as backing.
- `covered` is `customer_assets >= customer_liabilities`;
  `shortfall` is what is missing, `"0"` when covered.

Only posted balances count (drafts and holds do not). Accounts of
other types, and `own` accounts, never count. New `liability` accounts default to
`customer` and every other type to `own`, so until the backing asset
accounts are marked `customer` the report shows the full liability
as shortfall. The top-level `covered` is true when every asset is.

**As of a date.** Without `as_of` the report is read from the running
`account_balances`. With `as_of` it is rebuilt from the postings
whose transaction has `effective_at <= as_of` (posted or later
reversed, like `trial-balance?as_of=`) **using the `fund_class` and `liquidity` each
account had at `as_of`**: reclassifying an account afterwards does
not change the report for an earlier date. The class history comes
from the audit log (`account.update`), so a change made straight in
the database is not seen. A posting backdated into the period after
the report was first asked does change it: freeze a date with
`POST /v1/ledgers/{id}/coverage-snapshots`.

item.name: Freeze the coverage report at a date

request.description:
Stores the ledger's coverage report as of `as_of` (see
`GET /v1/ledgers/{id}/coverage?as_of=`) as an immutable snapshot with
a `snapshot_hash`: the SHA-256, in hex, of its canonical JSON
(`ledgercore.coverage.v2`: format, ledger, `as_of` in UTC and the
per-asset sums, `customer_claims` included, rows sorted by asset). Snapshots are append-only (the
database rejects UPDATE and DELETE), so the report a regulator
received for a month-end stays exactly that. Taking the same `as_of`
again adds another snapshot, with the same hash unless history
changed meanwhile. `as_of` is required and may not be in the future
(400 `validation_failed`). The daily `anchor-heads` also publishes
the id and hash of each ledger's latest snapshot. Requires
`ledger:write`.
Get a coverage snapshot

item.name: Freeze every account of a provider

request.description:
Freezes the custody, receivable and payable accounts of provider `P` in one database transaction, with the locks, modes, audit and events of `POST /v1/accounts/{id}/freeze`: nothing captures, dispatches or settles through `P` once the call returns, and no movement commits between the first account and the last. Requires the `ledger:write` scope. An account belongs to `P` when `metadata.provider` is `P` or its path has the segment `provider` followed by `P` (the rule of `GET /v1/provider-positions`; names compare in lower case). Only `asset` and `liability` accounts are frozen: expense accounts of `P` (fees, loss write-downs) stay open for bookkeeping. Parents of those accounts are frozen too, as in the account freeze. **Holders' wallets stay active.** Their money is a claim on the operator, not on `P`; they keep spending, paying and receiving. Which holders carry the loss is a separate decision, set by the ledger's loss-allocation rule: under `pro_rata_pool` nothing else moves when a provider is frozen and a loss is shared pro rata when it is recognized. With no rule set, nothing else moves either. **Under `by_provider`** the same transaction also moves each named holder's traced portion at `P` (its `P` share in `GET /v1/ledgers/{id}/exposure-matrix`) out of its wallet into `liabilities:holder::provider_claim:

`, a customer liability created when missing and frozen (`all`, same `reason` and `case_ref`): what the holder had at `P` can no longer be spent, and the rest of the wallet stays active. The wallet legs come from the holder's postable customer liabilities, `…:available` first, each up to what it has free of holds (held money stays). It is one posted transaction with reference `provider_claim:

`, booked with `frozen_override` and the freeze `reason` (a holder frozen on its own is moved too, and audited as `transaction.frozen_override`). The call takes the ledger lock exclusively, so it waits for the writes in flight and no write commits between the fold and the move. Freezing again moves only what is still traced to `P` in a wallet (nothing, after the first time); unfreezing leaves the claims frozen. A claim path that would turn an account with activity into a parent is 422 `parent_has_activity` and nothing is frozen. `mode` (`all` by default, `debits`, `credits`), `reason` (required, 1 to 1024 characters) and `case_ref` (optional, up to 128) are the same as on the account freeze. A provider with no account in the ledger is 404. The response lists every account of `P` after the change, followed by the claim accounts frozen by the call.

item.name: Reserve a provider's liquidity for a dispatch

request.description:
Creates a hold on `custody(P)`, the provider's custody account, so a
payout or dispatch reserves the provider's liquidity in the same
transaction as the stage that names it (ADR-020 section 3). It is
`POST /v1/holds` with the account chosen by the ledger: the hold, its
idempotency, expiry, events and `movement` tag are the same. Requires
the `ledger:write` scope.

Choosing `P` (preferred provider, cheapest, largest balance) stays in
the tenant's router; the ledger only checks that `P` can pay. The hold
is refused with 422 `insufficient_funds` when `P`'s available custody
(posted minus active holds) is below the amount, whatever the account's
`allow_negative`, and with 422 `account_inactive` while `P` is frozen
(`POST /v1/ledgers/{id}/providers/{provider}/freeze`). Concurrent
dispatches serialize on the custody balance row: they never reserve
more than `P` holds.

`custody(P)` is the one leaf `asset` account of the ledger that
identifies `P` (`metadata.provider`, or the `provider` path segment;
names compare in lower case), with `fund_class: customer` and
`liquidity: liquid`: the accounts `GET /v1/ledgers/{id}/provider-exposure`
counts as custody. A provider with none is 404; one with several is 409,
and the client names the account with `POST /v1/holds`. Send neither
`account_id` nor `ledger_id`.

item.name: Unfreeze every account of a provider

request.description:
Returns every frozen account of provider `P` in the ledger (same
selection as `POST /v1/ledgers/{id}/providers/{provider}/freeze`) to
`active`, whatever its mode, in one database transaction. Requires the
`ledger:write` scope. Accounts that are active or closed are left as
they are, so a retry changes nothing and emits nothing. `reason` is
required and `case_ref` optional; they go to the audit log
(`account.unfreeze`) and `ledger.account.updated`. A provider with no
account in the ledger is 404.

item.name: Freeze, unfreeze or close an account, or change its overdraft policy, fund class or liquidity

request.description:
Changes the account's `status`, `allow_negative`, `fund_class` and/or
`liquidity` (a `claim` is for assets only, 400 otherwise); send at least
one. Fields left out keep their value. Requires the
`ledger:write` scope. Every change also leaves an `audit_log` row
(`account.update`) with the previous and the new values.

- `active` <-> `frozen` move freely. A frozen account rejects every
  new transaction and hold (422 `account_inactive`); captures and
  releases of holds it already has still work.
- `closed` is **final**: a closed account cannot be reopened, frozen
  or have its policy changed (409 `conflict`).
- Only an **empty** account can be closed: zero posted balance, no
  active holds and no draft transactions pending in every asset it
  has touched. Otherwise 409 `conflict` — drain it, release or capture
  its holds and post or discard its drafts first.
- Lowering `allow_negative` to `false` on an account that is already
  below zero is accepted: it can be refilled but not taken lower.
- Only a postable account can be changed. A parent (`postable:
  false`) receives no movements, so its status and policy would govern
  nothing: 422 `account_not_postable` — change its children instead,
  or freeze the whole subtree at once with
  `POST /v1/accounts/{id}/freeze`.
- A `frozen` status set here is a freeze of mode `all` with no reason;
  to freeze only the debits or the credits, or to record a reason and a
  case reference, use `POST /v1/accounts/{id}/freeze`.

The change waits for the transactions and holds already in flight on
the account and blocks new ones until it commits, so a freeze or close
never lands between a movement's status check and its commit.

Every change emits `ledger.account.updated` with the new and the
previous values. A request that changes nothing returns the account
as it is and emits nothing, so retries are safe without an
idempotency key.

item.name: Freeze an account and everything under it

request.description:
Freezes the account **and every account under its path** in one database
transaction, so no movement commits between the first leaf and the last
and none commits on any leaf once the call returns. It works on a parent
(`postable: false`), which `PATCH /v1/accounts/{id}` refuses: call it on
a holder's parent account to freeze the holder's whole subtree (ADR-020).
Requires the `ledger:write` scope.

`mode` says which postings a frozen account still refuses, read against
the **direction of each posting**: `all` (the default) refuses every
posting; `debits` refuses DEBIT postings and accepts CREDIT ones (on a
wallet: the money going out is blocked, a deposit still lands);
`credits` is the opposite. Holds reserve money a later debit spends on a
credit-normal account, so they follow `debits` there. A refused posting
fails with 422 `account_inactive`. `frozen_override` still relaxes a
freeze of any mode.

`reason` is required (1 to 1024 characters) and `case_ref` is optional
(up to 128 characters, e.g. a compliance case number). Both are stored
on every account that changes, written to the audit log
(`account.freeze`, one row per account that changed) and sent in
`ledger.account.updated`.

Closed accounts are skipped. An account already frozen with the same
mode, reason and case reference is left as it is, so a retry changes
nothing and emits nothing; with another mode or reason, it replaces
them. The response lists every account of the subtree after the change.

item.name: Unfreeze an account and everything under it

request.description:
Returns every frozen account of the subtree (the account and everything
under its path) to `active`, whatever its mode, in one database
transaction. Requires the `ledger:write` scope. Accounts that are active
or closed are left as they are, so a retry changes nothing and emits
nothing.

`reason` is required (1 to 1024 characters) and `case_ref` is optional
(up to 128 characters). They are written to the audit log
(`account.unfreeze`, one row per account that changed) and sent in
`ledger.account.updated`; the accounts themselves keep no freeze state
once active. The response lists every account of the subtree after the
change.

Returns one balance row per asset the account has ever touched.
`pending` includes draft transactions and uncaptured holds;
`available` = posted - active holds against the account.

For a parent account (`postable: false`) the rows are the sum of its
whole subtree — every account whose name starts with the parent's
name followed by `:` — computed on read, never stored, and signed by
the parent's `normal_balance`; `version` is the sum of the members'
versions and `aggregate` is `true`.

request.description:
On a parent account (one with sub-accounts under its path) the list
covers the postings of its whole subtree. `metadata_key` and
`metadata_value` keep only the postings of transactions whose metadata

query.description: Metadata filter, used together with `metadata_value` (exact match).
Value `metadata_key` must have, exactly.
Page size; values above 200 are clamped to 200.
Opaque keyset cursor from a previous page's `next_cursor`. A

request.description:
Filters combine with AND. `account_id` keeps the transactions with a
posting on that account or, for a parent account, anywhere in its
subtree (404 if the account does not exist for the tenant).
`metadata_key` + `metadata_value` keep the transactions whose
metadata has exactly that pair (exact string match; both or neither).
The pair goes through the write-side metadata rules, so a key or value
that looks like personal data is refused with `metadata_pii_detected`
(422) and never echoed. Pagination is the same keyset on
`(created_at, id)` with or without filters.

Creates a balanced transaction. With `status=posted` (default) it is
atomically validated and posted; with `status=draft` it can be posted
later via `POST /v1/transactions/{id}/post` or abandoned via
`POST /v1/transactions/{id}/discard`.

`idempotency_key` is unique per tenant: retrying with the same key
returns the original transaction instead of creating a duplicate
(200 with the `X-Idempotent-Replay: true` response header). The key
may be sent in the body or via the `Idempotency-Key` request header.

A `frozen` account rejects new transactions (`account_inactive`). Facts
the platform must record whatever the customer does — a payout the bank
already paid, a chargeback the PSP already deducted, a seizure order —
carry `frozen_override`: it relaxes `frozen` (never `closed`) on the
accounts the transaction touches, needs the `ledger:frozen_override`
scope (403 without it) and a reason (400 without it), and leaves an
audited `transaction.frozen_override` row. Balance, overdraft, periods
and metadata rules still apply.
Get a transaction

Transitions a draft transaction to posted. Idempotent for
already-posted transactions. A reversed or discarded transaction
cannot be posted (409 `conflict`). Requires the `ledger:write` scope.

Transitions a `draft` to the terminal status `discarded`: its pending
amounts are released from the accounts' balances, it never receives a
journal number and never enters the hash chain, and the call leaves an
`audit_log` row (`transaction.discard`). Emits
`ledger.transaction.discarded`. The postings stay (they are
append-only) and are excluded by the status. No request body.

Allowed even when the draft's `effective_at` falls in a soft- or
hard-closed accounting period: it is the way out for a draft stuck
there. Idempotent: discarding an already-discarded transaction returns
it unchanged. A posted or reversed transaction cannot be discarded
(409 `conflict`); reverse a posted one instead. Requires the
`ledger:write` scope.

Creates and posts a new compensating transaction with mirrored
postings, links both, and marks the original as reversed.
The compensating transaction is announced with
`ledger.transaction.posted`, followed by `ledger.transaction.reversed`.

Reversing onto a `frozen` account is rejected (`account_inactive`)
unless the body carries `frozen_override` (a chargeback the PSP already
deducted must be recorded even if the customer is frozen); see
`POST /v1/transactions`. The audit row names the reversal and the
original in `reverses`.

`metadata` is copied onto the reversal and into
`ledger.transaction.reversed`, checked like a transaction's metadata
(scalars, no personal data, the ledger's `transaction_keys` allowlist).
It is part of the idempotency fingerprint: a retry with other metadata
under the same key is a 409. A reversal without `metadata` is
unchanged.

`movement` writes the reversal as a stage of a staged movement
(ADR-019); see `POST /v1/transactions`. A reversal does not inherit the
original's movement: when it touches a transit account it must name
one (422 `movement_required`), and it cannot take the movement's
transit below zero (422 `movement_transit_overdrawn`). A failure
before the movement ends is reversed with stage `fail` on the same
movement.

`amount` reverses only part of a single-asset transaction (a partial
chargeback). Each side's postings are scaled pro rata to it (largest
remainder), so a fee leg gives back its share; the reversal keeps
`reverses`. It needs an `idempotency_key` (the default key names only
the original). The original stays `posted` until the reversals in
force cover all of it; the one that does sets `reversed_by` and
`status: reversed`. Asking for more than is left is a 409; a reversal
itself is only reversed in full (400 `validation_failed`).
`ledger.transaction.reversed` carries `partial`, `asset` and `amount`
for a partial reversal.

`account_overrides` moves a leg of the reversal onto another account
of the same ledger (original account id -> replacement id), e.g. a
chargeback charged to another account of the same holder. The ledger
has no holder object (ADR-020), so "same holder" is the caller's
claim; the replacement is checked like any posting (status, freeze,
overdraft). Both fields are part of the idempotency fingerprint.

A side of a transfer between ledgers cannot be reversed alone: it is
refused with 422 `transfer_unbalanced`; use
`POST /v1/ledger-transfers/{id}/reverse`.

Reversing a reversal (a dispute won) gives the money back but leaves
the original `status: reversed`; `GET /v1/transactions/{id}` returns
the effective state in `reversal`.

request.description: List a ledger's accounting periods

Appends an `open` period `[starts_at, ends_at)` to a ledger. The
periods of a ledger are contiguous: the first one may start anywhere,
each next one must start exactly at the last one's `ends_at` (400
`validation_failed` otherwise), so they never overlap or leave gaps.
Dates outside every period are not governed, and a ledger without
periods behaves as if periods did not exist. Requires `ledger:write`.

Moves the period forward: `open` -> `soft_closed` -> `hard_closed`
(`soft_closed` may be skipped). Setting the current status again is a
no-op. Going back, including reopening a hard close, is 409
`conflict`. Each real transition writes a `period.transition` row to
the audit log in the same database transaction. Requires
`ledger:write`.

- `soft_closed`: only adjustments of this period
  (`adjusts_period_id`) may be dated in it.
- `hard_closed`: no transaction may be dated in it (422
  `period_closed`); correct it with an adjustment dated in an open
  period.

**Close checklist (6.19).** A response that leaves the period closed
carries `checklist`, read under the period lock: movements in transit
or in flight, transit residuals, active holds, pending adjustment
requests dated in the period, suspense balances and coverage gaps,
each with the age of the oldest. It is informational, except that a
hard close with adjustment requests `pending` or `approved` dated in
the period is refused (409 `period_pending_adjustments`): they could
never execute afterwards. Execute, reject or cancel them, or send
`force: true` with a `reason`; the override is in the audit row.

item.name: What is still open for a period

request.description:
The close checklist of the period, read now (see `PeriodChecklist`).
It is what `PATCH /v1/periods/{id}` returns when it closes the
period; ask for it before closing. Requires `ledger:read`.

request.description: Newest first. `status=pending` lists what checkers have to review. Requires `ledger:read`.

Records the complete proposed adjustment — postings, metadata,
`effective_at`, `adjusts_period_id` — made by the calling identity (the
maker), in status `pending`. It is judged now as a transaction would
be (accounts, metadata allowlist, period rules) and again when it is
executed. The server computes `request_hash` (SHA-256 of its canonical
form, see docs/maker-checker.md); after that the content never
changes. Two other identities must approve that hash before the
request can be executed. Requires `ledger:write`.

`idempotency_key` is unique per tenant: the same key and content
replays the request (200 + `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`); the same key
with other content is 409 `idempotency_conflict`.
The request with its approvals. Requires `ledger:read`.

Records the calling identity's approval of the `request_hash` it
reviewed. The maker cannot approve (403 `self_approval`), an identity
approves once (409 `conflict`), and the hash must be the request's
(409 `request_hash_mismatch`). The second approval moves the request
to `approved`. Only a `pending` request takes approvals. Audited.
Requires `ledger:write`.

`pending` -> `rejected`, final. Stopping a request moves no money, so
any identity with `ledger:write` may do it; rejecting a rejected
request is a no-op. Audited.

item.name: Cancel a pending or approved adjustment request

request.description:
`pending` or `approved` -> `cancelled`, final (e.g. the period was
hard-closed after the approvals). Cancelling a cancelled request is a
no-op. Audited. Requires `ledger:write`.

Writes the request's transaction, posted and never as a draft
(ADR-009), through the normal path
(period rules, metadata allowlist, overdraft, journal hash chain), with
idempotency key `adjustment-request:<id>`, and links request and
transaction (`transaction_id`). Exactly once: a repeated or concurrent
execution returns the same transaction (200 +
`X-Idempotent-Replay: true`). If the transaction is refused (e.g. the
period was hard-closed meanwhile) the request stays `approved`.
Audited. Requires `ledger:write`.

Reserves funds on an account (reducing `available` without moving
money) until captured or released.

`idempotency_key` is unique per tenant: retrying with the same key
returns the original hold (200 + `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`).

At `expires_at` the hold expires (ADR-016): a sweeper in ledger-core
(every `LEDGERCORE_HOLD_SWEEP_INTERVAL`, default 1m) moves it to
`expired`, frees the reservation and emits `ledger.hold.expired`.
Until then the funds stay reserved, but a capture or release past
`expires_at` is already 409 `hold_expired` (and frees them at once).

A hold is for short authorizations. A payout already sent to a bank is
not one: once the hold expires the funds are free to spend and the
bank's confirmation can no longer be booked. Book it through
`liabilities:payouts_in_flight:<provider>` instead
(`docs/payouts-en-vuelo.md`).
Get a hold

Finalizes the hold (fully or partially): the held funds are freed and
the hold is marked captured, optionally linked to the posted
transaction that moved the money. A partial capture releases the
remainder. Capture does not create the transaction itself — post it
via `POST /v1/transactions` and link it with `transaction_id`.
A hold past `expires_at` is 409 `hold_expired`, whether or not the
sweeper has already marked it `expired`.

`movement` writes the capture as a stage of the staged movement the
hold belongs to (ADR-019; 400 `validation_failed` when the hold belongs
to another one or to none). The movement's row is locked first and the
stage judged against its status; a capture that is refused (expired,
not active, stage too late) moves nothing.

Frees the reserved funds without moving money. A hold past
`expires_at` is 409 `hold_expired` (its funds are freed by expiry).

The optional body carries `movement`, which writes the release as a
stage of the staged movement the hold belongs to (ADR-019), judged like
a capture's.

Records an immutable rate between two assets: 1 unit of `base_asset`
is `rate` units of `quote_asset`, both in major units. A quote is a
rate, not an execution: it may back any number of posting groups
until `expires_at`, and it can never be changed or deleted. Not
idempotent: every call creates a new quote. Requires `ledger:write`.
Requires `ledger:read`.

Writes two or more posted, single-asset transactions atomically: all
members commit or none does. Each member goes through the normal
posting path (balance per asset, periods, metadata allowlist,
overdraft, account status, hash chain) and carries `posting_group_id`.
A member that mixes assets is 400 `validation_failed`. Requires
`ledger:write`.

With `fx`, the group cites an FX quote and a conversion account.
Across the members, that account's net movement in the base asset and
in the quote asset must be non-zero, of opposite sign, and the quote
amount must equal the base amount times the rate within one minor unit
(422 `fx_rate_mismatch`). The quote must not be expired
(422 `fx_quote_expired`). An invalid quote, rate or group is 400
`validation_failed`.

`idempotency_key` covers the whole group: the same key and payload
replays it (200 + `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`); the same key with
another payload is 409 `idempotency_conflict`. The key may be sent in
the body or via the `Idempotency-Key` request header. Members get the
derived keys `<key>/1`, `<key>/2`, ….
The group with its member transactions. Requires `ledger:read`.

request.description:
Every published version, newest first; `event_type` narrows the list
to one event type. Requires `ledger:read`.

Publishes the next version of the rule for `event_type` in a ledger.
A rule maps a canonical event to the lines of one transaction: each
line names an account (a fixed `account_id`, or an `account` role the
event fills), a `direction`, the name of one of the event's `amount`s
and, optionally, an `asset` (default: the event's). Rules are
immutable and versioned: publishing never edits an earlier version,
and each version carries a `rule_hash` over its event type, computed
amounts and lines.

Since ADR-027 a rule may also declare `computed` amounts (`sum`,
`sub`, or `mul` by a decimal `factor` with a declared `rounding`), lines
that repeat over a list of the event (`each`), and `signed` lines whose
negative amount books the other side, optionally on a
`negative_account_id` / `negative_account`. A rule without them
evaluates and hashes exactly as before.
Not idempotent: every call publishes a new version. Requires
`ledger:write`.
Requires `ledger:read`.

Applies the rule for `event_type` (the latest version, or
`rule_version` when given) to the event's `amounts` and `accounts` and
posts the resulting transaction through the normal posting path
(balance per asset, periods, metadata allowlist, overdraft, account
status, hash chain). The transaction carries `posting_rule_id`. An
amount of `0` skips its lines. `lists` feed the rule's repeated lines
(ADR-027); computed amounts are derived, never supplied. A rule with
`fx` (ADR-028) books a posting group instead, one member per asset
under the keys `<idempotency_key>/1`, `/2`, …, citing `fx_quote_id`;
such an event cannot settle a hold and its key is at most 240
characters. Every amount and role the rule names
must be supplied, and nothing else (400 `validation_failed`). The
postings must balance (422 `unbalanced_transaction`). An unknown
`event_type` or `rule_version` is 404. Requires `ledger:write`.

`hold_id` (optional) settles an active hold in the same booking: the
transaction captures it, as on `POST /v1/transactions`. A hold past its
`expires_at` is 409 `hold_expired`.

`idempotency_key` is required and may be sent in the body or via the
`Idempotency-Key` request header (the body field wins). The same key
and payload replays the event (200 + `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`).
The same key with another payload, or a key already held by a plain
transaction, is 409 `idempotency_conflict`.
The event with the transaction it booked. Requires `ledger:read`.

Moves value between two different ledgers of the tenant. A ledger never
holds an entry that crosses ledgers, so a transfer is two posted
transactions, one per ledger, written atomically: both commit or
neither does. Each side names its `ledger_id`, its `due_account_id`
(the inter-ledger due-to / due-from account of that ledger) and its
`postings`, and goes through the normal posting path (balance per
asset, every posting in its own ledger, periods, metadata allowlist,
overdraft, account status, hash chain). Both transactions carry
`transfer_id`.

The due accounts must eliminate: per asset, the net movement of the
source due account plus that of the target due account is zero, and
the source due account must move (422 `transfer_unbalanced`). Both
sides naming the same ledger, or a posting in the wrong ledger, is
400 `validation_failed`.

`idempotency_key` covers the whole transfer: the same key and payload
replays it (200 + `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`); the same key with
another payload is 409 `idempotency_conflict`. The key may be sent in
the body or via the `Idempotency-Key` request header. The two
transactions get the derived keys `<key>/source` and `<key>/target`;
if one of those is already held by another transaction the call is
409 `idempotency_conflict`. Requires `ledger:write`.

A side may swap the asset it received through a conversion account.
With `fx` (`quote_id`, `account_id`) the transfer cites an FX quote
and that conversion account, which belongs to either side; its legs
across both sides are judged exactly as in a posting group: opposite
signs and the quote amount equal to the base amount times the rate
within one minor unit (422 `fx_rate_mismatch`), quote not expired
(422 `fx_quote_expired`). Without `fx` nothing prices the conversion,
unless a ledger has `require_fx_quote` on: then a transfer that moves
more than one asset is refused with 422 `fx_quote_required` when
either of its ledgers has it (`PUT /v1/ledgers/{id}/fx-policy`). The
quote is part of the request for idempotency.
The transfer with its two transactions. Requires `ledger:read`.

item.name: Reverse both sides of a transfer between ledgers

request.description:
Reverses a transfer as a pair, in one call and one database transaction
(ADR-015, roadmap 6.22): a mirror transaction in each ledger, each
linked to its side by `reverses`, announced with
`ledger.transaction.posted` and `ledger.transaction.reversed` like any
reversal. Both commit or neither does, so the due accounts keep
eliminating at every step.

**A transfer is only reversed as a pair.** Reversing one side alone
with `POST /v1/transactions/{id}/reverse` is refused (422
`transfer_unbalanced`) and writes nothing: the database checks at
COMMIT that the due accounts still eliminate per asset once the
reversals of the pair are counted.

`amount` reverses part of a single-asset transfer, in the source
side's asset (the same rules as a partial reversal, 6.12); the target
side is scaled by the same proportion, rounded down. When the two
sides do not reverse equal amounts of the due accounts the whole call
is refused with 422 `transfer_unbalanced`. A partial reversal needs an
`idempotency_key`; without `amount` the key defaults to
`reversal-of:<transfer id>`. The sides' reversals are keyed
`<key>/source` and `<key>/target`: the same key and request replays
both (200 + `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`), the same key with another
request is 409. Asking for more than is left is a 409; reversing a
side already reversed is a 409.

`reason`, `metadata` (checked against each ledger's `transaction_keys`)
and `frozen_override` apply to both sides. Requires `ledger:write`
(and `ledger:frozen_override` for the override).

request.description:
The tenant's movements, newest first by `opened_at`. Every filter is
optional and they combine. To find the operations that have been going
for too long: `status=open&opened_before=<now minus the age>`.
Requires `ledger:read`.

Opens a staged movement (ADR-019): one operation of the tenant in one
ledger, such as a remittance or a payroll run. It starts in status
`open`; later steps of this feature move it forward and close it. The
ledger gives no meaning to `type` (the tenant's own label) or to
`reference` (the tenant's id for the operation, not unique).

`idempotency_key` is required: the same key and request replays the
movement already opened (200 + `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`); the same
key with another ledger, type, reference, quote or metadata is 409
`idempotency_conflict`. The key may be sent in the body or via the
`Idempotency-Key` request header. `metadata` follows the rules and the
`transaction_keys` allowlist of a transaction's. Requires
`ledger:write`.

`parent_movement_id` opens a **return** (a refund or chargeback) of a
`completed` movement of the same ledger (ADR-019 §6): 404 when it does
not exist, 409 `movement_stage_invalid` when it has not completed,
400 when it is itself a return. Its first write is usually a full or
partial reversal (`amount`) of the parent's `complete` transaction,
tagged with the return movement, which puts the money back in its
transit; it completes by paying the origin. The parent's `figures`
then net the return.

Closed strictly before this instant (RFC 3339); after `from`.

request.description:
Sums the revenue, cost and margin of the movements **closed** in
`[from, to)` (on `closed_at`), by `type` and asset (ADR-019 §5). Each
movement counts only its own writes: a return shows under its own type
(e.g. a negative margin under `refund`) and nothing is counted twice.
Grouping by a metadata dimension is roadmap 6.7. Requires
`ledger:read`.
Requires `ledger:read`.

Requires `ledger:write`. Makes the movement terminal with `outcome`
(ADR-019 §2, §4). `completed` needs the movement to have reached
`captured`; `failed` and `cancelled` are accepted from any status that
has not ended. In the same database transaction the close:

- releases the movement's still-active holds (`ledger.hold.released`
  with `reason: movement_closed`), so no reservation outlives its
  operation;
- computes the movement's transit per asset and, when it is not zero,
  records it as `transit_residual`. The close is **not refused** for a
  residual: the outcome is a fact. Only writes at stage `correct` can
  bring it back to zero (see `MovementRef`);
- emits `ledger.movement.closed`, with the residual (empty when none).

Idempotent by outcome, so it takes no idempotency key: closing again
with the same outcome returns the movement unchanged; another outcome is
409 `movement_closed`. A tagged write can also close its movement in the
same call with `movement.close`.

request.description:
The privileged actions this service recorded for the tenant (who, what,
when, with the minimum state before and after), oldest first, filtered
by date, action and resource. Each entry carries its place in the
tenant's hash chain (`chain_seq`, `prev_hash`, `entry_hash`; canonical

item.name: Check the tenant's audit hash chain

request.description:
Recomputes the whole chain and reports its head and every broken link:
`seq_gap` (a row is missing or numbers were rewritten), `prev_hash`
(the row does not link to the one before) and `entry_hash` (its
contents no longer hash to the stored value). `ok` is true when there
are none. The check runs inside the database, so a rewrite that also
re-hashes the rows after it passes; compare `head` with the head
published by the operator's `anchor-heads` / `audit-verify -anchor`
to catch that. Read-only; its cost grows with the tenant's trail.
Requires `ledger:read`.

Compute the balance as of this instant: the report is

request.description:
Sums debits and credits per account and asset over posted
transactions. For a healthy ledger, total debits equal total credits
per asset.

With `from` the report becomes a period result: each row sums only
the movements whose `effective_at` falls in `[from, as_of]`, so a
September salary does not leak into October. A transaction reversed
in a later period contributes its original postings to its own period
and the reversal's postings to the period of the reversal.

request.description:
`account_id` may be a parent account: the statement then covers its
whole subtree (a holder's history in one call), each entry carries the
`account_id` and `account_path` it hit, and balances are signed by the
parent's normal balance side. `metadata_key` + `metadata_value`
restrict opening, entries and closing to the transactions with exactly
that metadata pair, which is the balance of one order, employee or
category inside a shared account.

Statement of one account over a period: opening balance per asset
(aggregate of postings with `effective_at` strictly before `from`),
entries ordered by `effective_at` ascending with a per-asset running
balance, and the closing balance at `to`. Balances are signed by the
account's normal balance side, so a funded credit-normal wallet shows
positive numbers. Reversed transactions keep contributing (their
compensating transaction appears as its own entry). Entries are
keyset-paginated; opening/closing always cover the whole period
regardless of the page.

Net position against every counterparty (payment provider, bank,
processor), aggregated from the running `account_balances` of asset-
and liability-type accounts — never from postings.

Convention: an account belongs to a provider when its name/path
contains a `provider` segment followed by the provider name —
`assets:provider:acmepay:usd` or `liabilities/provider/nordpay/mxn`
(both `:` and `/` work as separators) — or when the account carries
`metadata.provider` as an explicit override (it wins over the path).

`net` is the signed sum of `posted_debits - posted_credits` across
the provider's accounts per asset: positive means the counterparty
holds value for us (`they_owe_us`), negative means we owe them
(`we_owe_them`), zero is `flat`.

Tenants that do not follow the convention get an empty `data` array
plus a `hint` explaining how to opt in.

item.name: Create a match rule version for a source

request.description:
Match rules say how a run pairs the source's statement rows with
ledger entries. Rules are **immutable**: each `POST` creates version
n+1 for the source (the first is version 1); to change the logic,
create a new version. A run records the version it used.

A source without rules runs the **built-in rule** (version 0, never
stored): 1:1 on the transaction idempotency key, exact amount, any
account, which is the behavior before rules existed.

`one_to_many` (one statement row settles several ledger entries) and
`many_to_one` (several statement rows pay one ledger entry) compare
sums inside a group, so they require `account_id`: the mirror holds
every leg of every transaction and a sum over both legs is
meaningless.

request.description: List a source's custody balance snapshots

Stores the balance a custodian (bank, PSP) reports for a ledger
account at a cut-off, next to the balance the posting mirror gives
for the same account and cut-off (ADR-011).

`ledger` = sum of debits minus sum of credits of every mirrored
posting on the account, in the asset, with `posted_at <= as_of`
(computed in SQL, it cannot wrap). It is only as complete as the
mirror: postings from before reconciliation consumed
`ledger.transaction.posted`, or history the stream lost, are missing.

Snapshots are **append-only**: a correction is a new snapshot. When
`reported` differs from `ledger`, the snapshot opens a `critical`
`balance_mismatch` discrepancy (`discrepancy_id`); otherwise
`discrepancy_id` is null. `difference` is `reported - ledger`.

request.description: List a source's settlement batches

Declares what a PSP reports for one settlement: `gross` captured,
`fees` kept, `chargebacks` and `refunds` netted, so
`net = gross - fees - chargebacks - refunds` is paid out. The batch is an
expectation that is checked, never consumed (ADR-011).

**Evaluation** runs when the batch is created and again on every run
of the source, while the batch is `open`:

- No statement row with `external_ref` equal to `batch_ref` yet: it
  stays `open` (captures and payouts arrive on their own schedule).
- The payout row exists, equals `net` in the batch asset, the
  ledger captures add up to `gross` and the linked reversals add up
  to `chargebacks + refunds`: `settled`.
- Anything else (wrong amount or asset, captures different from
  `gross`, reversals different from `chargebacks + refunds`, the
  payout repeated): `mismatched`, and a `high`
  `settlement_mismatch` discrepancy is opened (`discrepancy_id`).

`settled` and `mismatched` are final: the batch is never evaluated
again. **Captures** are the debit legs on `account_id` whose
transaction metadata `metadata_key` equals `batch_ref`; the ledger's
own payout booking (a credit on the same account) is not a capture.
**Chargebacks and refunds** are the credit legs on `account_id` of
*linked reversals* (`POST /v1/transactions/{id}/reverse`, full or
partial, which keeps `reverses` to the original deposit) whose
metadata `metadata_key` equals `batch_ref`: reverse the capture with
that metadata. The ledger cannot tell a chargeback from a refund, so
they are checked together against `chargebacks + refunds`; the split
is the PSP's declaration. Reversals mirrored before recon migration
`0013` carry no link and never count. The payout row is only
referenced, so matching still pairs it with the ledger's payout
posting (the default matcher pairs `external_ref` with the posting's
idempotency key, so the payout posting must use `batch_ref` as its
key, or a `group_by=metadata` rule must be used).

request.description: List a source's callbacks

Stores one provider event in the source's inbox (ADR-012). Providers
deliver at least once, so the same event arrives again on timeouts
and retries; each `event_id` is kept once per source.

- First delivery: `201` and the stored callback.
- Redelivery of a known `event_id` with the **same canonical
  payload**: `200` and the stored callback with `duplicates`
  incremented. Nothing is processed twice.
- Same `event_id` with a **different payload**: `409` (`conflict`).
  Either the provider reused an id or the payload was tampered with;
  the stored event is not changed.

The canonical payload is `event_type`, `occurred_at` (in UTC) and
`data` re-encoded with sorted keys and numbers kept verbatim. Key
order, whitespace and the time zone offset do not matter, so a
provider retry that only reformats the body is still a duplicate.

An event with `event_type` = `transaction` becomes a statement row of
the source (`external_id`, under its own import `callback:<event_id>`)
and the next run matches it like any CSV row (`status` `processed`).
Every other type is stored as evidence with no side effect (`status`
`ignored`). `data` of a `transaction` event needs `external_ref`,
`amount` (minor units, string) and `asset`, plus an optional
`direction`; anything else in `data` is kept as sent.

This route is behind the platform's JWT (`reconciliation:write`), for
a tenant integration that relays the provider's events. A provider can
also deliver directly, signed with the source's callback secret, to
`receivePublicCallback` (ADR-017); both routes share this inbox.
Stored events cannot be changed except for their duplicate counter.

Ledger idempotency: book the money with the bank's reference
(`external_ref`) as `idempotency_key`, never this `event_id`. A provider
resend with a new id becomes a second statement row, flagged `duplicate`
by the next run. See docs/aviso-proveedor-a-ledger.md.

item.name: Create or rotate a source's callback signing secret

request.description:
Generates a new signing secret for the source's public callback route
(ADR-017) and returns it **once**; it is stored only encrypted
(AES-256-GCM) and never shown again. Needs `reconciliation:write`.

- First call: `201`, `previous_expires_at` is `null`.
- Later calls rotate: `200`. The old secret keeps verifying until
  `previous_expires_at` (24 h), so the provider can switch keys
  without losing events. A second rotation inside the window drops
  the oldest secret at once.

Each call is written to the audit log without the secret.

Uploads a CSV statement as `multipart/form-data` (max 10 MiB) with
two fields:
  - `source_id`: UUID of a registered source
  - `file`: the CSV statement

Required CSV columns (any order, header row required):
`external_ref`, `amount`, `asset`, `occurred_at` (RFC 3339).
`amount` is a decimal string (e.g. `100.00`) converted to integer
minor units with an exponent of 2. The import is processed
synchronously; the response carries the final status.

Runs the matcher for one source over its unmatched statement rows
against the ledger entries not yet matched. The run executes
synchronously. It uses the source's match rule `rule_version`, or the
latest version when omitted (or 0), or the built-in rule when the
source has none; the run records the version it used.

`matched_count` and `unmatched_count` count **statement rows**, not
matches: a 1:N match of one row counts 1, an N:1 match of three rows
counts 3.

request.description: List discrepancies

Partial update: send only the fields to change. All of `status`,
`severity`, `owner` and `resolution_note` are optional, but at least
one is required (an empty body is 400 `validation_failed`).

- Changing `severity` moves `due_at` to `created_at` + the SLA of the
  new severity, so raising the severity of an old discrepancy can make
  it overdue at once.
- Moving `status` to `resolved` stamps `resolved_at`; moving it back to
  `open` or `investigating` clears it.
- `owner` is a handle (user id, team slug, `api_key:<id>`), never an
  email or a name: it is copied into the audit log, which holds no PII.
  Send `""` to unassign.

item.name: Rotate the signing secret (24h grace period)

request.description:
Generates a new secret and returns it exactly once. The previous
secret keeps VERIFYING until `previous_secret_expires_at` (24 hours):
during that window every delivery is signed with both secrets (two
`v1` entries in `X-LedgerCore-Signature`), so the receiver can switch
whenever it wants inside the window without losing events. After the
deadline the old secret is purged and never used again.
